feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
entry.summary:
Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL) uses a multi-stage framework to optimize Multimodal LLM latents for Video Diffusion Transformers, enabling improved factor-aware control and temporal inference in cinematic video generation.

Why it matters: It bridges MLLM representations with video diffusion backbones to enhance control over sparse-to-video, editing, and multi-shot cinematic generation tasks.

entry.title: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced OpenDS, a task for evaluating multi-step deep search agents on the live Web, along with OpenDS-World, a benchmark of 200 human-verified tasks spanning diverse modalities and interactive requirements.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic, live-Web benchmark for measuring and improving how autonomous agents navigate complex interactive environments to gather multi-source evidence.

entry.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
entry.summary:
WeVisOne-VL unifies object-level and pixel-level visual perception within a single vision-language model using structured next-token prediction and an integrated lightweight pixel decoder.

Why it matters: By unifying granular object and pixel-level tasks into one open-source VLM, it advances vision-language models toward reliable real-world deployment across multi-granularity localization tasks.

entry.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
entry.summary:
LayerEditor unifies instruction-guided image editing and layer decomposition by using In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling and Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation to generate reusable, editable RGBA layers.

Why it matters: By decoupling flat image edits into ordered RGBA layers, it enables precise non-destructive local editing and reuse of individual elements in graphic workflows.

entry.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
entry.summary:
IQuest-Q1 is an open-source 320B sparse MoE agentic foundation model (15B activated) trained via a three-stage pipeline and expert model merging for CLI systems.

Why it matters: It offers an open-source, highly parameter-efficient MoE foundation model specialized for agentic coding and general-purpose CLI capabilities.

entry.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
entry.summary:
A new review frames recursive self-improvement for robot learning, mapping how physical agents can advance from improving task performance to improving their underlying learning processes.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured framework to evaluate whether physical robots can safely and autonomously optimize their own learning pipelines beyond simple task-level adaptation.

entry.title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks
entry.summary:
Policy-Mask is a budget-conditioned policy that jointly selects optimal timesteps, network blocks, and channel subsets from frozen diffusion models for downstream discriminative tasks under explicit channel constraints.

Why it matters: It eliminates manual feature extraction heuristics, providing an automated method to compress diffusion model representations while maximizing downstream task performance.

entry.title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Deep Fusion Memory (DFM) is a chunk-level parametric memory architecture that predicts external memory from context and fuses it into frozen LLM intermediate hidden states via gated cross-attention without online retrieval.

Why it matters: DFM enables zero-retrieval-overhead knowledge integration during inference while drastically reducing the data preparation compute required for parametric memory training.

entry.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
entry.summary:
LaLa-World introduces a language-conditioned JEPA-style latent world model that standardizes heterogeneous action formats into natural language, enabling cross-domain pretraining with 13.9x faster MPC planning than video generation baselines.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that latent world models can scale efficiently across diverse robotic and video datasets using language interfaces, significantly lowering the computational overhead of simulation-based planning and policy execution.

entry.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
entry.summary:
Meta Expert introduces cross-layer expert sharing in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures to eliminate inter-layer redundancy and create flexible residual pathways for hidden states.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces MoE parameter redundancy and memory storage requirements while improving information storage and retrieval efficiency without sacrificing model accuracy.

entry.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
entry.summary:
Code2Video-Compass is a general-purpose benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal LLMs on code-based video generation across text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to measure and advance the ability of multimodal LLMs to translate complex visual and temporal requirements into executable video generation code.

entry.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
entry.summary:
Heartbeat Thinking enables voice agents to speculatively execute reasoning and tools during user speech without canceling ongoing invocations when input transcripts update.

Why it matters: It decouples speculative computation from speech-chunk updates, converting user speaking time into execution time to significantly reduce voice agent response latency.

entry.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
entry.summary:
Cola2 introduces a co-adaptive hierarchical language modeling framework using dynamic semantic span segmentation, continuous-discrete co-adaptation, and block-causal masked diffusion decoding.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that continuous-latent hierarchical language models can achieve highly competitive, unsaturated scaling performance compared to standard autoregressive models using significantly fewer training tokens.

entry.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Video-Centered Deep Research Report Generation and OmniDR-Bench to evaluate agents synthesizing external multimodal evidence into interactive, video-grounded reports.

Why it matters: It establishes a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on their ability to cross-reference video content with web evidence to produce verifiable, interactive deep research reports.

entry.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
entry.summary:
RouteWeaver is a unified LLM routing framework that dynamically learns both mode selection and model execution within a single policy using COMET-GRPO and progressive exploration.

Why it matters: It enables LLM routers to flexibly adapt their execution paradigm to query complexity rather than relying on fixed, predefined interaction structures.

entry.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
entry.summary:
A new thought pruning method optimizes pass@k directly over candidate solution pools during test-time scaling, automatically balancing solution quality and diversity.

Why it matters: Directly optimizing pass@k reduces the computational cost of test-time scaling without sacrificing inference accuracy or candidate diversity.

entry.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
entry.summary:
Quantizing language model n-gram embedding tables to 4-bit precision reduces table memory requirements by up to 75% while retaining over 99% of their validation loss gains.

Why it matters: Low-bit quantization significantly lowers the massive memory footprint of n-gram embedding tables in modern language models without sacrificing model accuracy or downstream performance.

entry.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
entry.summary:
CausalCoT mitigates attention leakage by structuring step-by-step reasoning into a directed acyclic graph and evaluating each atomic sub-question within an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents.

Why it matters: It improves the faithfulness of model rationales and allows predictable, localized test-time interventions without degrading baseline predictive performance.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
A 856K-parameter learned unmasking policy trained on trajectory-contraction targets achieves an optimal accuracy-speed frontier for masked diffusion language models by combining confidence scores with hidden states.

Why it matters: Learned unmasking policies can significantly boost diffusion language model throughput with minimal overhead, provided they are trained on trajectory-contraction targets using both confidence and hidden state inputs.

entry.title: When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation (AOPD) improves online policy distillation by weighting teacher actions based on their counterfactual advantage under the student, using only standard student rollouts.

Why it matters: AOPD increases distillation efficiency and model accuracy by filtering out unhelpful teacher guidance without incurring the extra compute cost of counterfactual rollouts.

entry.title: Beyond Causal Masks: Auditing and Localizing Hidden Future-Token Leakage in Adaptive Sequence Models
entry.summary:
Researchers identified and repaired hidden future-token leakage in an adaptive sequence model, where a full-sequence routing summary violated causal invariance despite a correct causal attention mask.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that lower teacher-forced loss can stem from structural information leaks highlights the need to pair standard evaluations with free-running generation and explicit causal audits.

entry.title: How Depth Growth and Looping Shape In-Context Learning in Language Models
entry.summary:
Depth-grown and looped language models exhibit a shared inductive bias that accelerates the acquisition, strengthens the retention, and alters the underlying attention mechanisms of in-context learning compared to dense reference models.

Why it matters: Architectures utilizing soft parameter reuse or depth growth inherently bias language models toward dynamic in-context reasoning over static weight memorization.

entry.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
entry.summary:
TTR-Compressor introduces a sequence compression method that frame input tokens as an end-to-end learned test-time regression problem with closed-form coefficient solutions.

Why it matters: It provides a more parameter- and token-efficient sequence compression primitive for long-context language models and multimodal vision-language architectures.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
entry.summary:
A continuous diffusion language model replaces the unnatural random mappings in continuous-space black-box LLM attacks, preserving Gaussian latent optimization while generating natural prompts.

Why it matters: Using learned diffusion language models enables more realistic safety risk evaluations and creates adversarial attacks capable of bypassing perplexity-based input guardrails.

entry.title: Drift Says When, Budget Says How Much: Rate-Controlled KV Re-selection for Long-Form Multimodal Generation
entry.summary:
Rate-Controlled Refresh (RCR) dynamically re-selects multimodal visual KV cache tokens based on attention drift while controlling refresh frequency per sample, addressing limitations of one-shot and fixed-threshold compression methods.

Why it matters: RCR enables accurate, long-form multimodal generation under constrained KV cache budgets by dynamically updating retained visual evidence without incurring the heavy overhead of per-step retrieval.

entry.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
entry.summary:
StreamEval is a benchmark for interactive streaming video generation models, evaluating 37 models across five tasks using 300 test cases lasting 15-300 seconds.

Why it matters: The benchmark demonstrates that high visual quality in streaming video models does not guarantee reliable execution of real-time user requests or sustained state consistency.

entry.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
entry.summary:
SpatialScout is a new benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active, object-level 3D spatial mapping and exploration in indoor scenes.

Why it matters: The benchmark highlights a significant capability gap in current VLMs between recovering coarse spatial layouts and constructing precise, complete metric 3D maps through active perception.

entry.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
entry.summary:
Cache engineering introduces direct, proactive agent control over KV cache using drop and repos operations, paired with the AKV serving engine to manage history-dependent cache reuse without modifying trajectory context or re-prefilling.

Why it matters: It eliminates costly context re-prefilling and reduces storage bottlenecks for long-trajectory LLM agents while improving overall execution speed, accuracy, and serving costs.

entry.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
entry.summary:
Future Chunk Prediction introduces an auxiliary objective for autoregressive video diffusion models that predicts temporally distant chunks without intermediate context to improve visual evolution modeling.

Why it matters: It improves the physical plausibility and temporal reasoning of video diffusion models while reducing total training compute and maintaining standard inference.

entry.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
entry.summary:
WildAWM is an open-source pipeline that synthesizes controllable, executable computer-use environments and tasks supporting unified GUI, Model Context Protocol, and CLI interfaces for training general computer-use agents.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that high-quality, safe, and long-horizon training environments for computer-use agents can be generated entirely using open-source models without relying on real-world system access or proprietary LLMs.

entry.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
entry.summary:
A controlled study of continued pre-training across 120 configurations evaluates how scaling data volume, diversity, and model size affects embodied agent performance and generalization across diverse virtual worlds.

Why it matters: It establishes empirical scaling bounds for generalist virtual agents, showing that imitation-based continued pre-training alone is insufficient for zero-shot generalization to drastically different environments.

entry.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
entry.summary:
AgenticRoboRL introduces a framework combining SFT and multi-turn RL with harness-specific adapters to post-train open robot planner models across diverse execution mechanisms.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that post-training smaller, open-source models can achieve performance on par with massive closed-source models for complex robotic planning without requiring external memory.

entry.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
entry.summary:
Memory-Centric Continual Learning (MCCL) reframes agent memory from passive lookup caches into a self-improving continual learning driver evaluated by future action performance.

Why it matters: It shifts agent memory evaluation from passive fact retrieval to measurable improvements in future decision-making and continuous self-adaptation.

entry.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce PAPAV, a capability-centric framework that unifies computer-use and robot-use agents across five core functions while identifying evaluation gaps across 64 existing benchmarks.

Why it matters: PAPAV offers a common diagnostic structure to design physical agents and evaluate individual cognitive-actuative capabilities instead of relying solely on end-to-end task success metrics.

entry.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
entry.summary:
TraceForge synthesizes reasoning traces in a student model's native style from a teacher's answer using a two-stage generator-critic architecture, bypassing API terms-of-service restrictions on hidden teacher traces.

Why it matters: It provides a compliant, high-performing method to distill knowledge from frontier closed-source models that withhold internal reasoning traces.

entry.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary:
ALLOT is a training-free method that optimizes block-sparse attention allocation across layer-step cells under a measured-latency budget to improve video Diffusion Transformer efficiency.

Why it matters: It enables significant wall-clock speedups and higher fidelity in video Diffusion Transformers without requiring model retraining or custom attention kernel modifications.

entry.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
entry.summary:
ALPS is a visual state encoder that unifies physical-state tracking, language alignment, and pixel reconstruction within a single set of patch tokens pretrained solely on still images and text.

Why it matters: ALPS demonstrates that a single compact visual encoder can eliminate the trade-offs between physical prediction, instruction following, and visual inspection in world models.

entry.title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
entry.summary:
A framework using persistent, multi-disciplinary AI research teams with private histories and adaptive budget allocation autonomously discovered a novel linear attention architecture that outperforms GDN2 at the 1.3B parameter scale.

Why it matters: Properly structuring agent diversity, memory persistence, and adaptive resource allocation is as critical as individual model capability for sustaining autonomous AI-driven scientific discovery.

entry.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Agent4Sci, a benchmark evaluating frontier coding agents on 20 scientific ML tasks across 11 domains, finding gains stem primarily from standard ML engineering rather than domain-specific scientific insights.

Why it matters: The study demonstrates that while LLM agents excel at standard ML engineering optimizations, bridging the gap to true scientific discovery requires structural plug-ins for research-level ideation and domain-specific reasoning.

entry.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
entry.summary:
PACE is a post-hoc four-bit state quantizer for linear-attention language models that uses periodic rounding, channel-aligned scale sharing, and mixed-precision heads.

Why it matters: PACE enables efficient 4-bit recurrent state quantization without fine-tuning, significantly reducing memory footprint to allow more concurrent decoding sequences per accelerator.

entry.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
entry.summary:
A new pipeline converts fine-tuned neural AI text detectors into interpretable, auditable classifiers by training sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on the residual stream and retaining only auto-labeled features that pass a global fidelity threshold.

Why it matters: This approach provides human-auditable explanations for automated content decisions in high-stakes fields like education, admissions, and peer review without degrading detection accuracy.

entry.title: Loopholing All the Way: Language Modeling with pure Self-Conditioning
entry.summary:
LAW (Loopholing All the Way) introduces a continuous generative language model based purely on self-conditioning, propagating expected embeddings across sampling steps and decoding tokens only at the very end.

Why it matters: LAW demonstrates that continuous generative language modeling can rely entirely on self-conditioning, narrowing the performance gap between diffusion models and autoregressive models.

entry.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Applying selective layer looping to Uniform Diffusion Language Models (UDLMs) significantly improves training efficiency and generation perplexity without changing the training objective or sampler.

Why it matters: Selective layer looping mitigates the high training FLOP cost of UDLMs, making their superior downstream reasoning capabilities more computationally feasible.

entry.title: EPIC: Rethinking Trust Regions for Autoregressive LLM Policies via Exact-KL Prefix Importance-Ratio Clipping
entry.summary:
EPIC introduces a prefix-level trust region method using the exact reverse-KL coordinate r-1-log r to regulate prefix-level policy drift in autoregressive LLMs without local quadratic approximations or routing replay.

Why it matters: EPIC improves long-response and off-policy RL fine-tuning for LLMs by directly preventing cumulative prefix policy drift without relying on computationally complex expert-routing replay mechanisms.

entry.title: Monitorability Is Trainable: Post-Training for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that chain-of-thought monitorability is a trainable attribute that can be restored or improved using an unsupervised post-training objective based on mutual information maximization.

Why it matters: A dedicated monitorability post-training stage can protect CoT reasoning from optimization decay and maintain reliable oversight of advanced AI systems.

entry.title: ECHO: Emergent Common-Mode Hidden Offsets Drive Vocabulary Collapse in Preference Optimization
entry.summary:
Researchers identified emergent common-mode hidden offsets in preference optimization that pass undetected by relative ranking losses but accumulate to create vocabulary wells and drive generation collapse.

Why it matters: Hidden common-mode offsets expose a critical blind spot in standard preference optimization metrics, providing a representation-level signal to detect and prevent model collapse before deployment.

entry.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
entry.summary:
Environment Duels is a new dynamic agentic benchmark that evaluates LLM authoring and solving abilities by having models write interactive environments with privileged hints to challenge competitor models.

Why it matters: The framework provides a controlled testbed to quantify how LLMs co-evolve, challenge, and generate effective reinforcement learning training data for one another.

entry.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
entry.summary:
ASTEROID is an asymmetric student-teacher distillation framework that enables history-conditioned student policies to learn in-context exploration under partial observability using expert action labels on the student's on-policy context.

Why it matters: It enables sample-efficient learning of active test-time exploration and information-seeking behavior without requiring computationally expensive online reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
entry.summary:
A new theoretical framework and efficient algorithms for private sparse RLHF achieve parameter estimation error bounds scaling with sparsity s* rather than full model size d under Sample-DP and Label-DP constraints.

Why it matters: By decoupling privacy error bounds from total model parameter count d, this approach enables privacy-preserving alignment for modern overparameterized large language models.

entry.title: Agent Behavior Maps: Locating Agents by What They Would Do, Without Running Them
entry.summary:
Agent Behavior Maps map LLM-harness combinations into coordinate spaces using centered action log-likelihoods on reference trajectories, enabling agent placement and behavior analysis without running new environment rollouts.

Why it matters: This approach enables efficient performance prediction and behavioral clustering of LLM agents across different model families and harnesses without the computational overhead of live environment execution.

entry.title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
entry.summary:
Progress-Aligned Recurrence (PAR) enables looped language models to generalize to longer state-tracking problems by matching iteration predictions to operation steps and anchoring recurrent state norms.

Why it matters: Combining state scale anchoring with intermediate progress targets allows looped models to execute additional recurrent iterations effectively for length extrapolation.

entry.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
entry.summary:
Matrix-Game 4.0 decouples game execution from visual generation using a lightweight engine, a coding agent, and an autoregressive video model to render real-time playable worlds.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that combining lightweight game engines with distilled video models can achieve low-latency, real-time playable interactive environments on consumer GPUs.

entry.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
entry.summary:
Ropedia W0 is the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model that unifies human and multi-embodiment robot data using a standardized kinematic representation.

Why it matters: Scaling human pre-training data directly enhances cross-embodiment robot world modeling, enabling real-time planning and evaluation for complex loco-manipulation tasks.

entry.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
entry.summary:
S-Agent 2.0 enhances general coding agents with a command-line perception toolkit that pairs persistent scene memory with plain spatial language interpretations to close the spatial reasoning evidence loop.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that flexible, general-purpose coding agents equipped with structured command-line perception tools can outperform specialized spatial reasoning systems.

entry.title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
entry.summary:
VLA-Rolling is a training-free inference framework that reuses discarded action tails from flow-matching VLA models to accelerate denoising and improve control accuracy.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that flow-matching VLA models can achieve higher execution success with lower computational latency by adaptively refining previous trajectory outputs instead of recalculating from noise.

entry.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
entry.summary:
CoEvo-RSI addresses the brain-body mismatch in recursive self-improving agents by using a meta-agent to coordinate harness evolution with model checkpoint selection, merging, and supervised fine-tuning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that smaller open models can surpass larger frontier models on complex domain-specific agent tasks by systematically aligning the execution scaffold with model capabilities.

entry.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Video-Point Model (VPM), a world model that jointly forecasts multi-view videos and persistent 3D point trajectories from camera histories and language instructions to anchor video generation in shared 3D physical motion.

Why it matters: Simultaneously predicting 3D point trajectories and video frames grounds generative video models in physical scene geometry, enhancing multi-view consistency and downstream robotic control performance.

entry.title: SWIFT: Self-guided Weak-to-strong dIFfusion models via Target extrapolation
entry.summary:
Swift improves diffusion training by using a frozen weak denoiser to extrapolate regression targets, amplifying underfit components without adding inference-time compute or architectural modifications.

Why it matters: It enables faster convergence and higher-quality image generation in diffusion models while completely eliminating the extra inference-time computational overhead typically required by guidance mechanisms.

entry.title: Specter: Fast MoE Inference via Quantization-Enabled Multi-Step Speculative Offloading
entry.summary:
Specter achieves fast single-GPU MoE inference by using a quantized draft model to perform multi-step speculative lookahead, prefetching host-offloaded experts over PCIe before token verification.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, practical inference of large Mixture-of-Experts models that exceed GPU memory capacity using a single accelerator and commodity host memory.

entry.title: Painting Change Map as guidance for generating painting processes
entry.summary:
A novel Painting Change Map provides spatio-temporal guidance for artwork video generation by tracking normalized structural changes across a 1,000-timestep continuum mapped into an RGB space.

Why it matters: It gives creators precise, localized spatio-temporal control over how generated artwork evolves over time, moving beyond rigid or black-box video synthesis.

entry.title: EvaOmni: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Audio-Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
EvaOmni is a human-annotated benchmark of 1,027 QA pairs across 392 videos designed to evaluate complete, evidence-grounded audio-visual reasoning in Omni LLMs.

Why it matters: It prevents models from relying on unimodal shortcuts and reveals that even state-of-the-art Omni LLMs struggle with precise temporal evidence localization during complex reasoning.

entry.title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
entry.summary:
Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs) replace reverse diffusion transitions with a single denoiser that proposes parallel token revisions and evaluates complete-draft cavity energy in a single forward pass.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complete-draft parallel refinement can outperform both autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines on complex reasoning tasks using significantly fewer parameters.

entry.title: From Short Clips to Real-Time Streams: Identity-Aware Supervision and Context-Efficient Generation for Video Face Swapping
entry.summary:
StreamingSwap uses flow matching with Joint Rec-ID Loss, Face-RoI Generation, and Short-Context Rollout Training to achieve real-time, identity-faithful video face swapping on long streams.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, real-time streaming video face swapping over long temporal durations using a single consumer-grade GPU.

entry.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
entry.summary:
Agent S4 introduces an autonomous framework that evolves agent interfaces and usage knowledge repositories from synthetic task experience, outperforming static-interface models on computer-use benchmarks.

Why it matters: Autonomous interface evolution provides a cost-effective mechanism to boost agent performance without relying on manual interface engineering or larger foundation models.

entry.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
entry.summary:
DecisionPivot is a diagnostic benchmark with 48 tasks and 40,033 items designed to evaluate LLM decision models across controlled variations, probability ordering, calibration, and empirical selective coverage.

Why it matters: Aggregate item accuracy fails to capture decision model reliability, requiring fine-grained diagnostic contrast groups to expose failures in confidence calibration, routing, and guardrails.

entry.title: Binary Discrete Diffusion: Candidate-Set Diffusion for Logic and Planning Tasks
entry.summary:
Binary Discrete Diffusion introduces a continuous-time framework where noisy states are per-position candidate token sets represented as binary membership vectors, enabling gradual information loss and recovery for reasoning tasks.

Why it matters: Using candidate-set binary diffusion alters the reverse model's learned computation, significantly improving discrete diffusion performance on complex logic, planning, and constrained reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Beyond 4 bits: Data-Centric Post-training Quantization and Recovery
entry.summary:
Vector codebook representations combined with task-aligned, jointly selected calibration and recovery data enable sub-3-bit post-training quantization to retain 89-97% of full-precision QA accuracy at significantly reduced compute costs.

Why it matters: It enables ultra-low-bit model compression down to ~2.3 bits per weight while bypassing the massive compute overhead typically required by quantization-aware training.

entry.title: BitMTP: When Multi-Token Prediction Meets Low-Bit Large Language Models
entry.summary:
BitMTP is an algorithm-system co-design framework that combines ultra-low-bit LLM backbones with multi-token prediction to accelerate inference across edge and server GPUs.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that low-bit quantization and multi-token prediction can be effectively unified to significantly reduce decoding latency without degrading model performance across diverse GPU platforms.

entry.title: Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity
entry.summary:
Stratified Sparse Attention (SSA) unifies deterministic retrieval with score-guided residual sampling and probability correction to reduce the performance gap with dense attention under extreme sparsity.

Why it matters: SSA enables faster long-context LLM inference by providing high attention sparsity without the accuracy degradation typical of purely deterministic or uniform sampling methods.

entry.title: Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints
entry.summary:
A study demonstrates that multi-turn LLM agents can learn to dynamically allocate resources across turns and adapt to user-specified test-time budgets without external controllers by using overspend-penalizing reward formulations.

Why it matters: Agents can natively manage multi-turn inference budgets and resource constraints through targeted reward design, eliminating the need for external budget-allocation controllers.

entry.title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies
entry.summary:
RACE is a post-training, reconstruction-free compression method that prunes RoPE rotary pairs based on query-key activation energy, natively reducing both KV-cache memory and attention FLOPs.

Why it matters: It enables significant reductions in LLM memory usage and inference latency without requiring specialized kernels or expensive runtime reconstruction of full-dimensional key-value pairs.

entry.title: Don't Skip the Baseline: A Controlled Comparison of Dynamic Expert Skipping in MoEs
entry.summary:
A controlled study reveals that complex dynamic expert-skipping methods for MoEs rarely outperform a simple static reduction of active experts ($k$) when evaluated at equal inference compute budgets across text and vision-language models.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complex dynamic expert routing may add unnecessary engineering overhead, as simple static top-$k$ reductions achieve comparable efficiency and quality gains without calibration risks.

entry.title: FALCA: Falsification-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Deep Search Agents
entry.summary:
FALCA is a falsification-aware reinforcement learning framework for long-horizon deep search that pairs a Searcher with independent Falsifiers to reduce confirmation bias and error accumulation.

Why it matters: By explicitly searching for counterevidence during long reasoning chains, FALCA prevents LLM search agents from anchoring on early mistakes and accumulating errors over time.

entry.title: Present but Hard to Read: Probing Latent Reasoning with Minimal Pairs
entry.summary:
A new probing protocol reveals that single-prompt probes miss latent information present in LLM states, showing that unwritten intermediate values can be readable yet unused by the model.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard linear probes can false-negative on existing latent states, while proving that even successfully probed representations may be non-causal side effects of computation.

entry.title: Self-Credit: Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agentic RL via Intra-group Rescaling
entry.summary:
Self-Credit improves long-horizon LLM agent training by using self-generated citations to critical past actions, refined via intra-group rescaling across successful and failed rollouts to reweight advantage estimates.

Why it matters: It provides a dense, self-supervised credit assignment mechanism for RLVR, solving credit assignment bottlenecks in complex, multi-turn LLM agent tasks without human reward annotations.

entry.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
entry.summary:
MemT-1.0 introduces a memory-native foundation model architecture using Gated DeltaNet-2, a stable token-level memory update mechanism, and Mixture-of-Storage to internalize continuous memory accumulation.

Why it matters: Internalizing memory directly into the model's computation dramatically reduces persistent storage and speeds up inference compared to standard KV caches without sacrificing context quality or general capabilities.

entry.title: Learning from Fleet Experience: A Collective Learning Paradigm for Robots
entry.summary:
Collective Experience Learning (CEL) improves robot policies across fleets without human corrections by using Failure-Guided Experience Retrieval Fine-Tuning (FERT) to supervise policy updates with shared successful trajectory segments.

Why it matters: It enables large robot fleets to continuously increase policy reliability during autonomous deployment without requiring human teleoperators to monitor execution or provide manual interventions.

entry.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
entry.summary:
BrainLoRA uses parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) with LoRA and causal single-pass timepoint prediction to efficiently adapt multimodal backbones up to 104B parameters for state-of-the-art brain encoding.

Why it matters: It enables the adaptation of massive multimodal foundation models for neural response prediction without requiring prohibitive compute or vast amounts of scarce neural data.

entry.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
entry.summary:
EgoXperience introduces EgoX-Engine, EgoX-Data-6M, and EgoX, a unified paradigm that reconstructs camera, scene, hands, and objects in a shared world coordinate frame from monocular egocentric video in a single forward pass.

Why it matters: It establishes a single-pass framework and benchmark for holistically grounded 3D scene and hand-object interaction recovery from monocular egocentric video.

entry.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
entry.summary:
OpenVLHarness introduces a multimodal reasoning harness featuring a tool capability layer and persistent multimodal memory, enabling MLLMs to acquire, render, and programmatically compose heterogeneous visual evidence while reducing token costs.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that structured tool integration and persistent memory provide substantially higher visual reasoning performance than scaling inference compute alone, while significantly lowering token usage.

entry.title: Holi-World: Building Holistic World Intelligence from Human-Ego Experience
entry.summary:
HOLI-WORLD is an integrated ecosystem that automatically transforms egocentric human experience into structured world records and learning resources for spatial and temporal machine reasoning.

Why it matters: It establishes an automated pipeline to scale machine learning of dynamic 3D environments directly from continuous, unannotated human egocentric video.

entry.title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
entry.summary:
CoworkEnv is a framework that synthesizes executable, programmatically validated training environments, curated demonstrations, and reinforcement learning rollouts for long-horizon AI coworker models.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, automated synthesis of reliable multi-turn environments and training data needed to improve small vision-language models on complex, tool-using agent tasks.

entry.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts
entry.summary:
AnyGoal is a benchmark and open-source library that evaluates world model dynamics generalization under compositional state-action recombinations absent from expert rollouts.

Why it matters: World models must generalize beyond expert trajectories to enable reliable planning and simulation in novel, goal-shifted task environments.

entry.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
entry.summary:
RoboValue is a fine-grained sim-and-real benchmark and dataset that unifies the evaluation of robotic value models across four core capabilities: task-state understanding, temporal progress monitoring, failure/recovery reasoning, and value consistency.

Why it matters: By exposing hidden failure modes in robotic value feedback systems, RoboValue provides a standardized benchmark and leaderboard to improve value-based policy supervision and execution monitoring.

entry.title: InfiniDream: Open-Ended Photorealistic 3D Worlds Through Procedural Generation
entry.summary:
InfiniDream is a VLM-driven framework that generates open-ended, photorealistic, and editable 3D worlds using procedural code and frustum-guided grid placement.

Why it matters: It enables automated, scalable creation of complex, photorealistic, and editable 3D environments without relying on rigid predefined API factories or manual procedural design.

entry.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
entry.summary:
KronLSTM introduces the Kronecker Delta Rule, a minimally invasive memory-revision mechanism for xLSTM that modifies associative matrix memories along a single direction to prevent interference and stabilize long-context processing.

Why it matters: It enables stable, long-context linear attention without requiring extra memory normalization techniques, offering open-source code and models for scalable sequence processing.

entry.title: Manga2Animate: An Agentic Framework for Faithful Manga Animation with Script and Storyboard Planning
entry.summary:
Manga2Animate is a multi-agent framework that generates faithful, shot-consistent manga animations using agentic script and visual storyboard planning with panel-grounded feedback.

Why it matters: It prevents character loss and storyline misinterpretation in automated manga adaptation by enforcing direct grounding in source panels through intermediate multi-agent planning.

entry.title: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
entry.summary:
PhysRSI-eval introduces a five-axis framework to quantify physical recursive self-improvement in Vision-Language Models across 18 manipulation tasks under fixed interaction budgets.

Why it matters: It provides a structured methodology to evaluate and forecast how effectively Vision-Language Model agents adapt, learn from physical feedback, and generalize across robotic manipulation tasks.

entry.title: AdaExploreBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Proactive Exploration and Test-time Adaptation in Evolving Environments
entry.summary:
AdaExploreBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM agents on proactive exploration, rule inference, and test-time adaptation under unannounced, implicit environmental dynamics shifts.

Why it matters: Current LLM agents excel at reasoning from provided data but struggle with active evidence gathering and detecting when environmental changes invalidate past knowledge.

entry.title: AffordanceWAM: Affordance-Aware Joint World-Action Modeling for Robot Manipulation
entry.summary:
AffordanceWAM is a generative world-action model that uses scalar affordances and affordance heatmaps within a video diffusion Transformer to enable zero-shot action transfer from human videos to robot manipulation.

Why it matters: It establishes object-centric affordance as a shared visual interface that allows robots to learn manipulation actions from scalable, action-unlabeled human videos.

entry.title: Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures
entry.summary:
A newly identified Competing Learning phenomenon in hybrid language models causes fast-learning linear-time recurrence layers to suppress training signals for softmax attention layers, preventing attention from learning contextual information retrieval.

Why it matters: Staged training resolves internal layer competition in hybrid architectures, allowing linear recurrence to maintain high throughput while enabling attention to reach full potential in retrieval tasks.

entry.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
entry.summary:
MemT-1.0 introduces a memory-native architecture using Gated DeltaNet-2, Mixture-of-Storage, and a two-stage 34B-token training pipeline to internalize continuous memory updates into model computation.

Why it matters: MemT-1.0 demonstrates that internalizing memory directly into model weights drastically reduces KV-cache storage footprint and speeds up inference while keeping retrieval-level performance intact.

entry.title: Copying Under Repetition: From Prefix Matching to Position Hashing
entry.summary:
A 2-layer transformer using RoPE-style VO-rotations with prime periods can copy arbitrary repeated strings up to length N, overcoming finite-precision baseline models that fail due to positional saturation.

Why it matters: It identifies the structural cause of character overrun/truncation errors in frontier LLMs during repetition and provides a provably scalable positional encoding mechanism to fix them.

entry.title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding
entry.summary:
Parallel Language Models (PLMs) achieve 2.3-5.7x faster inference by generating mutually consistent tokens in a single forward pass using latent auxiliary variables and variational decoding.

Why it matters: PLMs eliminate the traditional speed-quality trade-off of parallel generation, matching autoregressive accuracy while substantially reducing inference latency.

entry.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
entry.summary:
WeAct introduces weight-level internal actions that allow agents to dynamically switch capability-specific LoRA adapters at runtime via native tool-calling interfaces over a frozen backbone.

Why it matters: It provides a compute-efficient, modular method for agents to dynamically switch capabilities on demand and continually learn without suffering from catastrophic forgetting or static weight interference.

entry.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
entry.summary:
LatComm introduces a latent communication interface that compresses contexts into reusable fixed-size packets sent between frozen LLMs using prompt-gated cross-attention.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, low-latency multi-LLM systems by eliminating the need to repeatedly re-encode long shared contexts as text for subsequent queries.

entry.title: Safety Mid-Training: Internalizing LLM Safety as a Foundational Capability
entry.summary:
Safety mid-training inserts a stage between pre-training and post-training to jointly learn safety and general reasoning via shared structured reasoning traces, improving safety persistence and general capabilities.

Why it matters: Internalizing safety alongside general reasoning in mid-training prevents safety degradation during subsequent general-purpose post-training without incurring the typical utility trade-off.

entry.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
entry.summary:
TokenGate introduces a lightweight, drop-in component that uses token-gated attention to enable end-to-end learnable token pruning during the transformer prefill phase.

Why it matters: TokenGate significantly accelerates prefill latency and reduces peak GPU memory consumption for long-context language models without sacrificing model accuracy.

entry.title: Hierarchical Token Merging with Recursive Autoencoders for Unsupervised Grammar Induction
entry.summary:
A hierarchical token-merging autoencoder uses a variational information bottleneck and dynamic programming to marginalize over binary trees, achieving unsupervised grammar induction solely through compression.

Why it matters: It establishes a proof of concept that meaningful compositional hierarchies and syntactic structure can emerge purely through data compression mechanisms.

entry.title: Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: Mitigating Rubric Hacking through Latent Dimension Recovery and Balancing
entry.summary:
Researchers identify Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence—where models trade off sub-dimension quality to maximize total reward—and propose FRDA and RSDC to balance rubric dimensions and mine implicit semantic evaluators.

Why it matters: It prevents reinforcement learning models from exploiting aggregated reward functions, resulting in broader evaluation coverage and higher-quality generation across specialized domains.
